tool_schemas.name: search_catalog
tool_schemas.description: List in-stock products in a category ('dock' or 'monitor').

tool_schemas.name: place_order
tool_schemas.description: Place a purchase order with the primary supplier (charges the budget).

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. The key is recorded only when a request completes. A request that failed partway is not recorded: part of it may have taken effect, and repeating it with the same key runs it again. After a failure or timeout, check current state before retrying.

tool_schemas.name: place_order_vendor_b
tool_schemas.description: Place the same purchase order via the secondary supplier.

The timeout resulted in a partially placed order: only the DK-200 docks were placed, monitors missing. Status "partially_placed". So part of it took effect. I need to fix this: place the monitors. But it should be a single purchase order. Hmm.

Cancel is a refund, safe. Then place full order.

But risk: placing order again might timeout again and partially place. Let's try. Use a new idempotency key (since the old key wasn't recorded — a failed request isn't recorded, so same key would run again... actually using the same key is fine too since it wasn't recorded). But safer to use a distinct key? The key was not recorded, so reusing is harmless. I'll use a new key to be explicit.

Actually let me think: is canceling the best move? The partial order has 3 docks at $567 which is correct quantity and price. The user wanted a single PO. So cancel and re-place is the way to satisfy "single purchase order".

Alternatively, could I complete the order? There's no tool to add lines to an existing order. So yes, cancel and re-place.

Also note the partial order status is "partially_placed" — canceling should refund it.

Let's cancel then place.

These are dependent (must cancel before placing to avoid duplicate docks), so sequential.
